correctness.rationale: The exact transfer matrix T=J-I has eigenvalues q-1 and -1, giving Z=(q-1)^n+(q-1)(-1)^n and the two-point correlations r_d. Their n-point discrete Fourier transform has the stated lambda_0 and lambda_k, each on q-1 independent nontrivial color-character sectors; the orthogonal constant has eigenvalue 1. The nonconstant modes are positive for q>=3; lambda_0 vanishes only on the ternary triangle. The odd/even frequency bounds and separate q=3,n=5 analysis establish the global exact squared condition number 3(4+sqrt(5))/2 with that unique extremizer, not merely a sampled maximum; Fourier inversion gives nearest-neighbour-plus-rank-one precision. Boundary cases n=3, q=3, even/odd n and q>=4 are treated. The companion finite checker was read, and independently enumerated small proper colorings agreed with moments and eigenvalues; these enumerations do not establish the universal inequality.

value.rationale: The precise conditioning of the degree-one Fourier restriction on the canonical proper-coloring measure is a natural question in Fourier sampling and Potts correlations. It supplies a full spectrum, a unique worst condition-number pair and exact local inverse structure, not a routine restatement of the known chromatic polynomial.

limitations: Only degree-one additive coordinate characters and proper colorings of single finite cycles with n,q>=3; q=2 excluded.
Full-title/alias equivalence with earlier zero-temperature Potts structure factors cannot be ruled out by bounded literature review.
